subject: Post-demo: private deployment feasibility and evaluation plan
body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rishi <maya@fintechco.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@infra-inc.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: private deployment feasibility and evaluation plan

Hi Maya / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the suggested next steps for the Private/VPC evaluation so your infra and security teams can validate feasibility: 

1) What we showed today
- Private control plane with customer-managed networking (Redwood control plane runs in our managed tenant but connects to customer VPC via private endpoints).
- On-prem / air-gap option: customer owns key control artifacts, can opt-in to an air-gapped runtime with local artifacts and no egress.
- Example latency numbers on a 16k token model using our quantized runtime (demo profiles attached).

2) Key follow-ups we agreed to validate
- Network topology test: validate peering or PrivateLink equivalent between FinTechCo VPC and the Redwood control endpoints. Samir, your infra team should verify outbound-only TLS to 10.4.0.0/24 (we'll provide IP ranges).
- Control plane scoping: Laura will share the minimal control plane traffic matrix and the flow for model fetch, metrics, and KMS integration (HSM/KMS options covered).
- Air-gapped feasibility: we propose a short checklist POC where our on-prem package is deployed in a test VLAN with no internet egress — confirm if hardware (NVIDIA A40 / H100) is available.

3) Competitive notes we discussed (so you have a concise comparison for internal stakeholders)
- Hyperscalers (Bedrock/Vertex endpoints): pros are broad cloud integrations and marketplace procurement; cons are less deterministic inference pricing and limited private air-gap options without heavy engineering.
- Vendor-hosted inference APIs: usually fast to start but often lack deterministic routing/fallbacks and fine-grained KV cache control we showed (useful for low-P50 latencies).
- Where Redwood sits: predictable throughput SLAs for reserved pools, explicit batching/cache controls to tune unit economics, and a private deployment model that supports both VPC control-plane patterns and full on-prem air-gapped runtime.

4) Proposed 3-phase evaluation plan (timeline estimates underneath each item)
- Phase A (Week 0–2): Network connectivity & security review (Samir/infra + Redwood ops). Deliverables: IP allowlist, TLS fingerprinting, control-plane traffic matrix.
- Phase B (Week 2–5): Private POC — deploy control-plane connectors into FinTechCo's staging VPC; run 100 rps synthetic load and a subset of your production prompt patterns. Deliverables: perf report, token cost estimates, trace logs for 1k requests.
- Phase C (Week 5–8): Air-gapped on-prem trial (if Phase B is good). Deliverables: binary/VMs for runtime, KMS/HSM integration guide, and a short runbook for upgrades and audit logs.

5) Risks & mitigations
- Risk: KMS/HSM integration timeline could add 2–3 weeks. Mitigation: we can run interim tests with ephemeral keys and provide audit-only mode.
- Risk: Network egress policy at FinTechCo blocks necessary telemetry. Mitigation: we can operate in a ‘metrics-only’ pull model or deliver sanitized logs via secure SFTP.

6) Next concrete steps (action owners)
- Samir: confirm a point-of-contact on infra and a tentative date for network test (target: week of Dec 8).
- Laura: send the control-plane traffic matrix and minimal IP / port list by EOD Dec 3. (Attachment: redwood-private-arch-diagram.pdf)
- Maya: share the 3 representative prompt sets and expected SLA targets for POC by Dec 4.
- Vivek / Aditya: we'll load the POC config and a cost estimate into the HubSpot deal record.

Attachments: redwood-private-arch-diagram.pdf (architecture sketch), fintech-poc-checklist.xlsx (POC checklist for infra/security)

Thanks — looking forward to the infra test.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2026 18:05:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: private deployment feasibility and evaluation plan

Vivek —

Thanks for the thorough recap. This looks good. A few clarifications from our side after the demo: 

- For the air-gap option, can you clarify what "no egress" means for license/heartbeat checks? Our security team will want to know if there is any periodic call-home and if so how it can be disabled.
- On KMS, we currently use a managed HSM with key rotation. We need to understand your integration surface and if key material ever leaves our boundary.
- Cost: please include an estimate of token costs for 50k tokens/day in Phase B (mixed 2k/8k prompts).

Samir will coordinate the infra folks. We can target Dec 9 for the network test.

—Maya
Maya Rishi
Head of Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
maya@fintechco.com
